docsPromises.evidence:
PARTIALLY RESOLVED, re-verified by execution, not by reading the diff. Fix commit 32a083b987 lands three of the sites this review originally flagged: (1) cli-engine.ts:1068 now derives its diagnostic source label from BRAND_ENV_PREFIX -- live-reproduced after a clean rebuild: `PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=999999 node bin/proof-or-stop.js done_prepare ...` prints 'source=PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS', AND `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS=999999` (deprecated spelling) still resolves and prints the identical line -- read-both is intact, no regression on the multi-developer guarantee. (2) checklist.ts:774 template-interpolates BRAND_ENV_PREFIX -- confirmed by loading the actual compiled packages/main/dist/core/brand-env.js and rendering the exact template expression: 'PROOF_OR_STOP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS' (did not force a live timeout to trigger the throw path itself; confirmed via the compiled constant instead, since forcing a genuine command-timeout is expensive and the string derivation is otherwise deterministic). (3) CLAUDE.md:77 and :844, docs/guide-hooks.md:33 now read 'PROOF_OR_STOP_SESSION_BRIEF_FRESH_MINUTES' / 'PROOF_OR_STOP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / PROOF_OR_STOP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS' first, with the deprecated name explicitly noted as still-read -- confirmed by direct file read, matching the commit's stated diff exactly.

NOT RESOLVED, and disclosed as deliberately out of this fix's scope: (a) packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:2296 has an un-derived literal 'LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS' in a dispatch-blocked user-facing nextAction string -- this is the exact same bug class as the two sites that were fixed, sitting in a file this story's own diff already touches elsewhere (57 lines changed in lattice-dispatch.ts), yet this specific line predates and survives the story's diff unchanged. (b) docs/guide-hooks.md's 'Environment Variables' table (lines ~86-96) and its four copy-pasteable shell examples (Telegram/tar/webhook snippets around lines 108, 137, 153, 169) teach ONLY the LATTICE_STAGE/LATTICE_STORY_ID/LATTICE_OLD_PHASE/LATTICE_NEW_PHASE/LATTICE_COMMAND/LATTICE_ERROR/LATTICE_RESULT_JSON/LATTICE_ARGS_JSON spellings -- zero occurrences of any PROOF_OR_STOP_* hook-injected counterpart anywhere in the file, even though packages/main/src/core/hooks.ts:buildHookEnv already dual-writes both spellings for every hook var (verified: applyBrandEnv/setBrandEnv calls at hooks.ts:76-90). This is a doc-only gap (the runtime already works correctly for either spelling) but the doc is in this story's own active-doc scan roots and was already edited by this story's diff (30 lines changed in docs/guide-hooks.md) without addressing this half of it. (c) CLAUDE.md's own core/debug.ts template example (LATTICE_SHELL) and Bridge-interface comment (window.__LATTICE_WS_PORT, CLAUDE.md:198,220) are a materially different case: __LATTICE_WS_PORT is a genuine, live, hardcoded (non-readBrandEnv) runtime identifier used in 5 real source files (browser-executor.ts, browser-client.ts, verifier/serve.ts, verifier/browser-client.ts) that inject/read a literal window global -- it has no read-both resolver at all, so 'renaming' it is a materially bigger change than the other three (a wire-format/protocol-level rename, not a diagnostics-string edit), and reasonably belongs in a scoped follow-up rather than this fix. I record it as accurately out-of-scope-for-this-specific-fix rather than resolved.

Judgment: the coordinator's disclosed non-sweep of LATTICE_SHELL/__LATTICE_WS_PORT is a reasonable scoping call (materially different, protocol-level surface). The disclosed non-sweep of docs/guide-hooks.md's hook-env-var table is NOT purely a follow-up matter: it is the same active doc, same file, already opened by this story's diff, teaching a still-incomplete promise. The lattice-dispatch.ts:2296 literal is also in-scope (same fix's stated intent, same file already touched by the story) and was simply missed, not deliberately deferred with the same rationale as the other two.

closingSelfCheck.summary: Second-pass re-review after fix commit 32a083b987: the LATTICE_* diagnostic-output drift I flagged in the prior round is genuinely and mostly fixed, re-verified BY EXECUTION (rebuilt dist, ran the exact env-var reproduction both with the canonical and the deprecated spelling to confirm no read-both regression, and loaded the compiled brand-env constant to confirm the checklist.ts template renders the canonical names). Three of the four sites originally flagged (cli-engine.ts:1068, checklist.ts:774, CLAUDE.md:77/:844 + docs/guide-hooks.md:33) are fixed and confirmed correct. This is NOT a full resolution of the underlying class of drift, and I am not marking it fully delivered: lattice-dispatch.ts:2296 has an identical un-derived 'LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS' literal in a file this story's diff already otherwise touches, and docs/guide-hooks.md's entire hook-injected-env-var table and four code examples still teach only the deprecated spelling despite the runtime already dual-writing both names -- both are disclosed by the fix's own commit message as deliberately not swept, but I judge the guide-hooks.md gap and the lattice-dispatch.ts literal to be in-scope for this story (same active-doc scan root already opened by this diff / same file already touched with the identical bug pattern), not a legitimate follow-up-story deferral, whereas the LATTICE_SHELL/__LATTICE_WS_PORT non-sweep IS a reasonable scope boundary (a hardcoded, non-brand-env-resolver, protocol-level identifier used by 5 real runtime files, materially bigger than a diagnostics-string edit). Everything else previously verified (bin dual-alias, freeze boundary, residue/process-fact/prompt-baseline/entrypoints/audit-scan gates, tsc clean) remains verified and unaffected by this round's changes.
